To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Grb10, a recently identified adapter protein, interacts with the insulin receptor in an insulin-dependent and substrate-1-independent manner.

we identified and isolated the SH2 domain of Grb10 and showed that it binds to the insulin receptor in a hormone-dependent manner, that the interaction requires an intact insulin receptor carboxy terminus, and that it is independent of insulin receptor substrate- 1.

Grb10 binds to the insulin receptor car-boxyl terminus in a hormone-dependent manner, that the interaction is mediated by the Grb10-SH2 domain, that the insulin receptor car-bxyl terminus is required for Grb10 interaction, and that Grb10 does not associate with insulin receptor substrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins that interact with insulin and insulin-like growth factor (IGF) receptors.
the identification of Grb10 and its interaction with the insulin receptor.
the identification of novel insulin receptor interacting proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Grb10, a novel insulin receptor substrate-2 (IRS-2)-related protein, binds to the carboxyl-terminal domain of the insulin-like growth factors (IGF) I and insulin receptor β-subunits and that it is a substrate for the IGF I and insulin receptor tyrosine kinases.
Grb10 binds the insulin receptor through its SH2 domain and that the interaction is dependent on the phosphorylated carboxyl termini of insulin receptors.
Grb10 binds to the carboxyl-terminal tail of the insulin receptor, and that it is a new component of insulin signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insulin receptor interacts with Grb10 in an insulin-dependent and substrate-1-independent manner via its C-terminus.
Grb10 binds to the insulin receptor in an insulin-dependent, SH2 domain-dependent manner.
we have identified a novel SH2 domain-containing protein, Grb10, that binds the insulin receptor in a hormone-dependent and SH2 domain-dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Grb10 adapter protein is a novel insulin and insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor interactive protein that binds to the insulin receptor β-chain through its SH2 domain.
Grb10 binds to the insulin receptor in a hormone- and SH2 domain-dependent manner.
the Grb10 protein interacts with the insulin receptor, which may have important implications for understanding insulin action.
